current CMake dependency/test declarations needed to classify the next groups.

The census finds 244 ROS packages: 107 have canonical package-local definitions
and matching root overrides; 137 lack those definitions. There are 243
ament_cmake packages and one ament_python package. Definitions are an adoption
inventory, not proof that every optional branch, original test, tool or resource
has been integrated. Keep the exact package assignments in UNIVERSE_COVERAGE.md
and sequence/acceptance policy in PLAN.md rather than duplicating full lists.

Pattern: assign each pending package once to a related dependency group, check
manifest prerequisite direction, and inventory the actual CMake/source/test/
launch contract before implementing it. Phases 9.2–9.19 cover radar, shared
providers, CPU perception, localization, motion/planning/control, GPU/model
consumers, system behavior, evaluation/simulator adapters and remaining RViz
plugins. Phase 9.20 reconciles all 244 package contracts with evidence, including
the baseline 107; 9.21 checks affected composed products and distributions.
Related packages may share an execution batch, while module commits and complete
suite gates remain separate. Model/SDK/device requirements stay visible; missing
prerequisites keep a task incomplete. No future patch or version is selected by
this inventory.

Know-how: inspect manifests across the whole source tree, not only the next
category. Shape estimation has conditional CUDA/TensorRT support, and calibration
status classification also requires TensorRT, so their groups cannot be declared
complete using CPU compilation alone. Existing occupancy-grid and behavior-path
manifests name pending preprocessor/sampler providers; these are audit leads,
not proof that an unused dependency must be added to current targets. Inspect
actual optional/public contracts when those providers enter the graph. A
manifest graph does not capture every CMake, runtime or dynamically loaded edge.

Reproduce the census and the ledger assignment/prerequisite checks from the
repository root (standard Python only; no Bazel server or SDK required):

```sh
rg --files src/universe/autoware_universe -g package.xml
python3 - <<'PY'
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path
import re
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET

root = Path('src/universe/autoware_universe')
packages = {}
for path in root.rglob('package.xml'):
    manifest = ET.parse(path).getroot()
    name = manifest.findtext('name')
    assert name not in packages, name
    packages[name] = (path, manifest)
ledger = Path('docs/bazel/UNIVERSE_COVERAGE.md').read_text()
entries = re.findall(r'\[([^\]]+)\]\(([^)]+/package\.xml)\)', ledger)
assert Counter(name for name, _ in entries) == Counter(packages.keys())
for name, link in entries:
    assert (Path('docs/bazel') / link).resolve() == packages[name][0].resolve()
existing = {name for name, (path, _) in packages.items()
            if all((path.parent / f).exists()
                   for f in ('MODULE.bazel', 'BUILD.bazel'))}
overrides = dict(re.findall(
    r'local_path_override\(\s*module_name = "([^"]+)",\s*path = "([^"]+)"',
    Path('MODULE.bazel').read_text()))
for name in existing:
    assert overrides[name] == str(packages[name][0].parent)
phase = None
assigned = {}
for line in ledger.splitlines():
    if line.startswith('### Phase 9.'):
        phase = tuple(map(int, line.split()[2].rstrip(':').split('.')))
    match = re.match(r'- \[ \] \[([^\]]+)\]', line)
    if match:
        name = match[1]
        assert name not in assigned
        assigned[name] = phase
assert set(assigned) == packages.keys() - existing
for name, group in assigned.items():
    for dependency in packages[name][1]:
        if dependency.tag == 'depend' or dependency.tag.endswith('_depend'):
            if dependency.text in assigned:
                assert assigned[dependency.text] <= group, (name, dependency.text)
print(len(packages), len(existing), len(assigned))
PY
```

Result: `244 107 137`; every package has one ledger entry, each pending package
has one phase, all existing pairs have matching overrides, and no pending-package
manifest dependency points to a later group. Local Markdown paths/phase anchors
and whitespace were checked as well. This one-time planning check is not a
build-time interface/source completeness validator. No Bazel build, runtime,
GPU, DDS, simulator or export checks were run: source, build definitions and
accepted configurations are unchanged. The next implementation task is 9.2;
refine its complete original/ROS gate before starting. Phase 8 remains deferred.

## 2026-11-23: Phase 9.3 — Local glog prerequisite

Purpose: satisfy autoware_glog_component from the available glog 0.6.0 snapshot
under src/universe/external/glog, not a different registry source. This selects
the same local provider for rosdistro's shared logging SDK and existing Agnocast
containers, so acceptance includes those consumers. Inspect the existing native
Bazel macro, complete CMake Linux test declarations and scripts, public headers,
logging/signal sources, rosdistro cc:glog ownership and container logging calls.

Pattern: add a glog module with gflags 2.3.1 (the selected SDK version),
rules_cc 0.2.26.rcr.0, GoogleTest 1.18.0.bcr.1 and rules_python 2.4.5. Keep the
old com_github_gflags_gflags spelling as gflags's module repo_name so the existing
macro resolves the same provider. Select it with a root local override before container consumers, and retain the
snapshot's own source/header-template generation. Update legacy native C++ rules
(including its example) to rules_cc loads for Bazel 9. Preserve gflags support,
custom prefixes, native logging, mock logging, symbolization, stack traces,
utilities and all three cleanup executables. The 13 original native/example
executables and two driver targets are required. CMake installation/configuration
self-tests describe CMake's own artifact contract, not the Bazel SDK output;
validate the actual Bazel shared provider and its consumers separately.

Diagnosed setup issues and resolutions:
- The native macro omits Linux glob support and read/write locks. Logging tests
  cannot compile without HAVE_GLOB_H; nested mock logging deadlocks with the
  fallback exclusive mutex. Enable these actual Linux features in the build.
- HAVE_UNWIND_H alone supplies no x86_64 trace backend. Enable the ABI unwinder
  using HAVE__UNWIND_BACKTRACE and retain logging frames with -fno-inline: the
  legacy unwinder skips a fixed number of frames. Reject unsupported-driver
  zero exits instead of treating them as stacktrace/signal coverage.
- Allocation-hook death tests require their new-expressions to execute. Compile
  the native test translation units at -O0; keep all assertions and cases.
- Cleaner tests need their surrounding repetition/count checks, original argv[0]
  names (logging uses them for file prefixes) and trailing-slash directory
  contract. A generic package-owned Python adapter runs the same three repetitions,
  delays and file-count assertions as cmake/RunCleanerTest1–3.cmake. Another
  adapter supplies the temporary .libs layout for the unchanged signal shell
  driver and rejects its unsupported/skip output.
- The original signal test prints pthread_self with 0x%px, creating 0x0x...x
  instead of the real signal-handler TID. Use %p; the shell driver's original
  equality check then passes. This is a test formatting bug, not a library
  implementation change. Upstream glog v0.7.1 uses a stream-formatted thread ID;
  its corrected approach is related, not an identical local patch.

```sh
  --test_timeout=60 --test_env=RMW_IMPLEMENTATION=rmw_cyclonedds_cpp \
  --test_output=errors @glog//...
```

separately from build support as 4108604f. Fixture roots use the canonical

common. Supply image_transport's package index through the ROS header/library
provider: its shared library initializes a plugin loader before main, even in
a helper-only test. Without the index that test aborts before assertions.

Demonstrated implementation failures: the fast voxel helper accepts non-finite
x/y because a comma expression discards their checks, producing two output voxels
instead of one for the mixed-validity fixture. Replace that comma with &&. Its
centroid stores intensity in the fourth vector element; multiplying that vector
by a homogeneous transform scales translation by intensity. A mean intensity of
20 yields x=200.5 instead of 10.5 for a 10-unit translation. Transform xyz with
homogeneous coordinate 1 while preserving intensity. Both public-API regressions
fail before these corrections; the transform case additionally checks rotation.
Upstream main retains both defects on 2026-11-23. Open Universe PR #13398 exactly
matches the transform correction; the finite predicate is outside that PR.
Keep the source corrections separate from Bazel definitions.

Lyrical exposes removed message_filters .h includes, then the one-argument
Subscriber template and QoS-object subscription API. Use canonical .hpp headers;
select the one-argument RCLCPP subscriber on rclcpp major 32+, retaining the
older template branch. Pass a QoS object on that standard path and the original
profile to wrapper subscribers. Preserve queue depth and SensorDataQoS policy.
The external crop-box test exercises plain, exact-index-sync and approximate-
index-sync delivery, including no output before matching indices, payload fields
and timestamp preservation, in both selected runtime modes. AWF trackers
#7404/#1538 and relevant Universe PR searches were reviewed; #13331 is the
related FilterBase feature, not this compatibility fix. Older ROS distributions
are not locally qualified by this gate.

The standalone fast-voxel target keeps its CMake dependency boundary (PCL,
pcl_conversions, rclcpp and sensor messages), with a shared transform-info header
provider. Its regression target uses that smaller runtime closure; image
transport is needed only on the ROS filter side. Also replace removed
pcl/io/io.h with pcl/common/io.h, which declares the used getFieldsList API.
Current upstream retains the old include; a scoped literal-header PR search
finds no match. The focused filter-base build passes after these compatibility
changes, but completion still requires the full gate below.

Test setup lessons: expose the ROS component manager library and package index to
the original characterization driver. Its 56 cases include actual load/unload
and timed behavior. test_blockage_diag's namespaced main is not a C++ entrypoint;
use the original CMake gtest_main contract. The Python launch test needs the
rclcpp_components ament_package (installed container executable), not just its
index. Explicitly carry image_transport's index in the preprocessor index too:
a component loaded by another process cannot inherit a C++ consumer's data edge.
The unchanged distortion suite exposes rounded-quaternion conversion failures
in its dependency; see the managed-transform-buffer entry and source fix
05309f1d. Preserve its existing numerical tolerances.

The Python suite initially fails six scenarios despite correct coordinates:
expected and actual sensor clouds appear in different row orders. Production
concatenation traverses an unordered_map and promises no sensor order. Upstream
Universe PR #13619, merged and checked 2026-11-23, corrects this exact assumption.
Align the original test with its fixture-specific sort_points helper and
assert_allclose calls. The fixture has integral sensor y/z positions; round
those stable keys to order clouds while motion compensation changes x. Keep
all eight scenarios, point counts and numerical tolerances. Three external
negative checks establish that the sorted assertions still reject missing,
duplicated or changed points and preserve tolerance/empty-shape behavior.
Do not impose an ordering change on production code to satisfy the old test.

```sh
env -i HOME="$HOME" PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin" \
  bazel test --keep_going --config=runtime --config=no-agnocast --local_test_jobs=1 \
  --test_env=RMW_IMPLEMENTATION=rmw_cyclonedds_cpp --test_output=errors \
  @autoware_pointcloud_preprocessor//... \
  //bazel/tests:pointcloud_preprocessor_behavior_test \
  //bazel/tests:pointcloud_fast_voxel_test \
  //bazel/tests:pointcloud_concatenate_core_example_test \
  //bazel/tests:pointcloud_concatenate_component_test \
  //bazel/tests:pointcloud_comparison_test

env -i HOME="$HOME" PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin" \
  bazel test --config=runtime --local_test_jobs=1 --strategy=TestRunner=local \
  --run_under=//bazel/agnocast:with_heaphook \
  --test_env=RMW_IMPLEMENTATION=rmw_cyclonedds_cpp --test_output=errors \
  //bazel/tests:pointcloud_preprocessor_behavior_test

readelf -d bazel-bin/external/autoware_pointcloud_preprocessor+/concatenate_without_ros_node
```

Standard result: all 118 non-test module targets and 21 test targets build;
185 original C++ cases across 16 groups, all eight original Python scenarios,
four external polygon/crop-box cases, two voxel regressions, three comparison
checks and the standalone example pass, zero failures/errors/skips. Final gate
16.8 s, reusing unchanged passing C++ results; the Python launch suite takes
12.8 s and comparison checks 1.5 s. The example's DT_NEEDED entries contain only
the compiler/C runtime and libm, with no RCLCPP, ROS TF or PCL ROS library.
Enabled result: all four polygon/crop-box cases pass in an Agnocast-only context
with the built heap hook and kernel device, zero failures/errors/skips, in
17.5 s (test 1.4 s). The test asserts RCLCPP stays uninitialized and covers plain,
exact and approximate index synchronization. Targeted formatting, Python AST,
shell syntax and diff checks pass. This completes the CPU preprocessor module;
it does not qualify GPU filters, Fast DDS or a complete sensor pipeline.
Local source correction: e7221ecc; Bazel definitions and added checks are
committed separately. Next: both IMU nodes and their complete original suite.

## 2026-11-24: Phase 9.5 — shared CPU filter-base provider

Purpose: preserve the original preprocessor's SHARED filter-base contract when
an independent ground-filter package starts consuming it. Inspect the original
CMake filter-base source/dependency list, existing Bazel aggregate headers and
the consumer's linked-but-not-exported diagnostics. Acceptance: complete original
preprocessor suite, existing external checks, enabled crop-box transport, and the
actual ground-filter consumer gate. The complete gates below pass.

Failure/cause: using the complete preprocessor plugin DSO as the base owner also
captures CGAL/GMP/MPFR, map/PCL and compiled utility archives through the broad
header provider. Bazel rejects consumer links because those transitive libraries
are already embedded but not exported. The original CMake contract requires a shared base owner.

Pattern: separate filter.hpp and utility/memory.hpp into filter_base_headers,
keeping the physical include tree for sibling includes. Its dependencies match
the helper API, without map/CGAL/filter-plugin dependencies. Compile filter.cpp
and memory.cpp once; publish pointcloud_preprocessor_filter_base_shared with a
unique library basename. The six contained compiled utility providers are
explicit roots, so native consumers can resolve their direct references from
one owner. Keep ROS/PCL and managed-TF globals in existing shared SDK providers.
Expose filter_base_runtime_dynamic_deps for downstream compiled consumers; the
main preprocessor runtime delegates to the same owner. Include the base library
in the package index alongside the original plugin/core libraries. Components
use logical module labels, with no dependency on product/runtime labels.

Both provider and consumer tests remain unchanged except the separately
qualified ground portability fixes. Reuse the previously passing tiny fast-voxel
and node-free core results when their action inputs remain unchanged. The shared
base boundary affects the original plugin/component suites, so rerun that full
module gate rather than assuming a successful link proves runtime correctness.

```sh
env -i HOME="$HOME" PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin" \

  --run_under=//bazel/agnocast:with_heaphook \
  --test_env=RMW_IMPLEMENTATION=rmw_cyclonedds_cpp --test_output=errors \
  //bazel/tests:pointcloud_preprocessor_behavior_test \
  //bazel/tests:scan_ground_filter_transport_test

readelf -d bazel-bin/external/autoware_ground_segmentation+/libautoware_ground_segmentation.so
```

Result, 2026-11-24: all 25 combined test targets pass, zero failures/errors/skips.
The provider retains all 185 original C++ cases, eight original Python scenarios,

passing results after the one-time provider recompilation; component

so empty retained clouds do not index element zero of an empty vector. All four

policy of discarding all low-confidence points. Radius-enabled mode passes
before this correction; both profiles pass afterward without weaker assertions.
Wait for both input subscriptions to be discovered before checking that mismatched
stamps produce no output. This avoids confusing discovery with synchronization.

Test-lifecycle failure/cause/fix: each original test passes all assertions, then
segfaults during process exit. A diagnostic GDB run locates rcl_logging_external_
shutdown/spdlog registry destruction with an active global ROS context. The
original bodies initialize RCLCPP but never shut it down. Close the context at
the end of each of the four original cases, preserving every assertion. Normal
Bazel test execution then exits cleanly. GDB's own exit code can mask a child
signal, so the debugger run is diagnosis, not acceptance evidence.

Production failures/cause/fix, reproduced by the nonempty scenarios:

- Dynamic 10 m cells fail with an out-of-range vector access: the array uses
  horizontal cell count times vertical physical cell size. Allocate horizontal
  count times vertical count, with null entries for unloaded cells. Guard null
  neighbors before lookup; retain actual loaded cells. This also makes sparse
  map coverage explicit instead of creating empty, non-null placeholders.
- The two KD-tree variants omit the cell-origin remainder used by the base
  voxel loader. Shifted cells (min x/y -5, width/height 10) are stored and queried
  in different slots. Initialize both origin remainders in their overrides.
- The distance-only dynamic path compares squared KD-tree distance with a
  linear threshold. Compare against the squared threshold, matching static mode;
  a point 0.6 m away must remain with a 0.5 m threshold.
- Lanelet sampling computes 1/num_samples with integer division, putting every
  sample at the segment start. Use 1.0/num_samples; a straight road then has
  valid elevation coverage at its interior, not just near boundary endpoints.

The external peer sends modern PointXYZIRC clouds with nonzero stamp and finite,
dense input. Static/dynamic modes remove near-map points and retain obstacle/
out-of-map points with original fields and order. Dynamic fixtures provide the
real differential-map service and odometry, 10 m cells offset from zero, unloaded
cells, a boundary-neighbor point and the 0.6 m threshold regression; require an
actual service request. Elevation comparison keeps the above-grid obstacle and
rejects ground/out-of-map points. Lanelet mode uses a declared flat LaneletMapBin
and writable cache with map coverage required, retaining the near-road point
and rejecting height/out-of-map points. Verify coordinates and frame/stamp.

sampling. The representative original test still lacks shutdown. Scoped PR

Purpose: let the trajectory modifier install its generated temporal-solver

combined DefaultInfo set; files declared dynamically with actions.declare_file

with headers (.h) and sources (.c). Consumers project these through ordinary

srcs. This is generic SDK support under third_party/acados, with no dependency

integrator generated_solver target; its public include path remains unchanged.

```sh
  --test_output=errors @acados//:tests
```

and the generated integrator solve (status 0, x0=1, finite terminal within .01
of zero). The projected inputs compile/link to identical passing test artifacts,
so Bazel reuses their unchanged runtime results. Generated headers remain in

or deployment gate is required by this provider-only metadata change.

## 2026-11-26: Root local dependencies without placeholder versions

Purpose: make root declarations express local source selection without a
redundant dependency version. Inspect the root MODULE, all included MODULE
fragments, existing local overrides and dependency conventions before editing.
The root has 345 local overrides, each paired with a bazel_dep at 0.0.0.
The included fragments introduce no additional local overrides.

The placeholder followed the package-dependency convention and allowed the
root to select the actual source. It does not contribute to resolution when a
local override is active. Bazel's
[migration guide](https://bazel.build/external/migration#introduce-local-repositories)
documents versionless bazel_dep/local_path_override pairs. Its
[non-registry override rules](https://bazel.build/external/module#non-registry-overrides)
exclude the overridden module from registry version resolution, including
published versions requested transitively. Missing local sources fail without
registry fallback. Only the consumer root's overrides apply.

Remove version = "0.0.0" only from root bazel_dep declarations whose module
names have a local_path_override. Keep each pair adjacent and preserve its
path and ordering. Keep package-local module metadata and dependency versions.
Keep registry declarations, including 0.0.0 dependencies whose concrete releases
are selected by the pinned RCR graph. Removing those versions is a different
resolution change. The steady-state pattern lives in DEVELOPING.md under
Dependency declarations. AGENTS.md and the adoption checklist link to it.

Before editing, save MODULE.bazel to
/tmp/autoware-local-versions-before.MODULE.bazel and capture representative
Core, Universe, asset and registry target locations. Repeat after editing:

```sh
bazel query --output=location \
  'set(@autoware_vehicle_msgs//... @autoware_trajectory_ranker//... @autoware_map_asset//... @rclcpp//:rclcpp)' \
  > /tmp/autoware-local-versions-before.locations
# Remove only the redundant versions from local pairs.
bazel query --lockfile_mode=error --output=location \
  'set(@autoware_vehicle_msgs//... @autoware_trajectory_ranker//... @autoware_map_asset//... @rclcpp//:rclcpp)' \
  > /tmp/autoware-local-versions-after.locations
sort /tmp/autoware-local-versions-before.locations > /tmp/autoware-local-versions-before.sorted
sort /tmp/autoware-local-versions-after.locations > /tmp/autoware-local-versions-after.sorted
diff -u /tmp/autoware-local-versions-before.sorted /tmp/autoware-local-versions-after.sorted
git diff --exit-code -- MODULE.bazel.lock
git diff --check
```

Results: both queries pass on Bazel 9.3.2. All 59 target locations match, and
the lockfile remains unchanged. A one-time Python AST comparison removes only
the local dependencies' version keywords from the saved manifest and compares
the complete resulting AST with the edited manifest. They match exactly.
The same audit checks all 345 adjacent pairs, their existing MODULE.bazel
paths, and all 345 materialized external repository symlinks against the
selected checkout directories. All pass. No source-selection or syntax failure
occurs. No persistent validator is added for this mechanical edit.

No compilation or runtime suite is rerun. The dependency sources and targets
remain unchanged, so their existing module acceptance results still apply.
No Fast DDS, simulator or deployment gate is selected. Phase 9.11 remains in
progress at 171/244 packages. Continue with its behavior-velocity plugins.
